description: Every script in this repository that an agent or a person may run. The safety class is one of read-only, local-write, remote-write, or human-only. An agent never runs a human-only entry. A later MCP server lists only the tools whose mcp_exposure is expose.

safety_classes.read-only: Reads files, git, or the network. Changes nothing.
safety_classes.local-write: Changes files in the working tree, a clone tree, or the factory records on this machine.
safety_classes.remote-write: Pushes, comments, labels, or opens a pull request.
safety_classes.human-only: Publish, deploy, spend, login, or secrets. An agent never runs it.

exit_codes.1: a check failed, a read failed, or a phase is unknown (a gate that times out is killed with its process group and reports exit 124 in the message, and the script exits 1)
exit_codes.2: wrong use of the script (a human-only step run without a terminal also exits 2)

mcp_exposure.expose: The MCP server lists the tool.
mcp_exposure.hidden: The MCP server never lists the tool. This is the default when the field is missing, so a new tool stays out of the server until someone marks it. A human-only tool must be hidden.

tools.name: gates
tools.description: Run the gates listed in release.config.json (the same list as release gates) in order. Record the real exit code of each. Print one line per gate.

arguments.name: --ci
arguments.description: Run npm ci first.

arguments.name: --bail
arguments.description: Stop at the first failing gate.

arguments.name: --cwd
arguments.description: The top folder of a work tree of this package. Default: the current folder.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, status, exit, path, gates: [{ name, command, exit, signal, ok, firstFailingLine? }] }. Exit 0 all passed, 1 a gate failed or git is missing, 2 wrong use.
tools.writes: node_modules (with --ci), dist, storybook-static, release-artifacts, and the docs-site build output, all inside the folder. The commands get an allowlist environment and a throwaway HOME.

tools.name: pr-open
tools.description: Check the pull request title and body, then open a DRAFT pull request with gh. It never opens a ready pull request.

arguments.name: --title
arguments.description: One line, at most 256 characters.

arguments.name: --body-file
arguments.description: A regular file of at most 64 KB, inside the repository or the temporary folder.

arguments.name: --base
arguments.description: The branch to merge into.

arguments.name: --dir
arguments.description: The top folder of a work tree of this package. Default: the current folder.

arguments.name: --expect-identity
arguments.description: The gh login that must be signed in. The tool stops if gh reports another one or cannot read it.

arguments.name: --dry-run
arguments.description: Check the text and print the command. Do not call gh.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, status, exit, draft, command, url } or { ok, status: 'invalid-body', exit, problems }. Exit 0 opened, 1 the text or gh failed, 2 wrong use.
tools.writes: Opens one draft pull request on GitHub through gh, as the identity it prints first. Writes no local file.

tools.name: tree-clean
tools.description: Check that a clone tree is clean, pushed, and idle. It refuses a tree whose own git config has a key that can make git run a program. It removes nothing.

arguments.name: <tree>
arguments.description: The top folder of a clone tree of this package.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, status, exit, path, removes: 'nothing', checks: [{ name, ok, detail }] }. Exit 0 all three pass, 1 a check failed, 2 wrong use.
tools.writes: Nothing is written. It runs git status, git stash list, git rev-list, and lsof on the machine, and git ls-remote, which is a network read of the remote tags.

tools.name: release status
tools.description: Read the version, the tags, and the registry, and list what is left.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, command, status ("pass" | "unknown" | "fail" | "usage"), exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }], warnings? } plus { package, version, phases: [{ name, state ("done" | "todo" | "unknown"), note }], left: [...], unknown: [...] }. Exit 0 pass, 1 when any phase is unknown or a read fails, 2 wrong use.
tools.writes: Network reads only (npm view and git ls-remote). It writes no file: npm gets a throwaway HOME, cache, and log folder that are removed at the end, and git never takes an optional lock.

tools.name: release preflight
tools.description: Check the config, the version rules, the publish workflow, the docs edition, the branch, and the clean tree.

arguments.name: --force
arguments.description: Run the step again even if it is recorded as done.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, command, status, exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }], ... }. Exit 0 pass, 1 a check failed, 2 wrong use. Adds commit.
tools.writes: Runs git fetch, which updates FETCH_HEAD and the remote-tracking refs inside .git. Writes release-state.json inside .git.

tools.name: release gates
tools.description: Run npm ci and every gate in release.config.json, then check the design kit and the built docs.

arguments.name: --force
arguments.description: Run the step again even if it is recorded as done.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, command, status, exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }], ... }. Exit 0 pass, 1 a check failed, 2 wrong use. Adds commit.
tools.writes: Runs npm ci, which replaces node_modules, then the gates, which write dist, storybook-static, release-artifacts, and the docs-site build output. Writes release-state.json inside .git only when the tree is clean before and after.

tools.name: release dry-run
tools.description: Run npm publish --dry-run, then check the package facts, the design kit zip, and the built docs.

arguments.name: --force
arguments.description: Run the step again even if it is recorded as done.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, command, status, exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }], ... }. Exit 0 pass, 1 a check failed, 2 wrong use. Adds commit.
tools.writes: Uploads nothing. Writes release-state.json inside .git only when the tree is clean after.

tools.name: release publish
tools.description: Print what a person does to publish. The tag starts .github/workflows/publish.yml. The script never runs npm publish.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, command, status, exit, message, steps, commands, blockers }. Always prints and never runs the commands. Exit 2 without a terminal, 1 with a terminal when not ready, 0 with a terminal when ready.
tools.writes: Nothing. It runs npm view (a read) and prints. It runs no write command.

tools.name: release verify
tools.description: Read the registry, install the package into a clean temporary project, and load every entry. Check the design kit and the built docs.

arguments.name: --allow-unsandboxed
arguments.description: Accept a Node without the permission model: the import of the registry package then runs without a file read limit, and a warning says so.

arguments.name: --force
arguments.description: Run the step again even if it is recorded as done.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, command, status, exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }], ... }. Exit 0 pass, 1 a check failed, 2 wrong use. Adds commit, exports, recorded.
tools.writes: Creates and removes a temporary project outside the repository. Writes release-state.json inside .git only when the tree is clean.

tools.name: release tag
tools.description: Print the exact git tag and git push commands for a person. The script never runs them, because a pushed tag starts a real publish.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, command, status, exit, message, steps, commands, blockers }. Always prints and never runs the commands. Exit 2 without a terminal, 1 with a terminal when not ready, 0 with a terminal when ready.
tools.writes: Nothing. It runs git ls-remote and other reads, and prints. It runs no write command.

tools.name: release retire
tools.description: Print the commands in release.config.json that retire the old alpha (deprecate it, remove the next tag), after a note that this is the owner's decision. The script never runs them.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, command, status, exit, message, steps, commands, blockers }. Always prints and never runs the commands. Exit 2 without a terminal, 1 with a terminal when not ready, 0 with a terminal when ready.
tools.writes: Nothing. It runs git rev-parse and npm view (reads) and prints. It runs no write command.

tools.name: release claims
tools.description: Find text that says the package is not published. Fail when a configured path is missing.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, command, status, exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }], ... }. Exit 0 pass, 1 a check failed, 2 wrong use.
tools.writes: Nothing. It runs grep on files in the repository.
